request.state: The image is a full PvP matchup introduction from The Bazaar. The streamer hero is the illustrated character on the LEFT. The opponent ghost hero is the illustrated character on the RIGHT. Ignore the real person in the webcam, usernames, titles and rank badges. Identify the underlying hero from visible character artwork using the option descriptions, allowing cosmetic skins. Never infer identity from the streamer person, opponent username or game items. Evaluate each side independently. Choose obstructed only when the hero artwork itself is hidden enough to prevent identification; choose unknown when visible artwork cannot be confidently identified as a listed hero.

streamer_hero.instructions: Which underlying hero is depicted in the LEFT illustrated character artwork? Select one hero, unknown or obstructed. Cosmetic skins preserve hero identity.

criteria.Dooley: A small robot liberator with a rounded mechanical body and one large circular lens/display in place of a human face. The central eye-like display is the strongest recurring cue; its expression, glow, shell, limbs, headgear, and orange scarf can change across skins.
criteria.Vanessa: A human-looking female pirate and swashbuckler, usually with a sharp-featured face, dark hair, and a confident or fierce expression. Her default portrait has swept black hair and red-and-black clothing, but hair accents, hats, masks, outfits, and weapons vary across skins; do not require pirate headgear or a particular weapon.
criteria.The Dragons: A musical duo: singer Rin and guitarist Jin, depicted together as youthful, pointed-eared, horned humanoid performers rather than a literal dragon. Default art contrasts Rin's warm pink complexion and bright orange-blond hair with Jin's cool blue-gray complexion, dark hair, and prominent pale curved horn; a tight crop may show only one member. Their paired identity is established, but comprehensive alternate-skin coverage was not verified, so do not require these exact colors or both faces to be visible.
criteria.Pygmalien: A large, broad-built anthropomorphic boar merchant with a pig snout, protruding lower tusks, pointed animal ears, and usually a beard or goatee. The snout-and-tusk face is more reliable than his default brown hair, blue clothing, jewelry, or pale fur collar, all of which can be altered or obscured by skins.
criteria.Jules: A four-armed, pointed-eared female chef and mother, with purple/lavender skin and long purple-magenta hair in the default art. Her chef's toque, apron, utensils, clothing, and hair styling are costume cues rather than requirements, and a face-only portrait will not reveal all four arms.
criteria.Mak: A human-looking male master alchemist, recognizable in default art by a strong angular face, dark full beard, thick brows, and glowing gold eyes. His white hood and green-and-gold robes are common default cues, not mandatory features; clothing, headgear, and other cosmetic details vary across skins.
criteria.Stelle: A human-looking, dark-skinned female engineer and aviator, with reddish-brown hair and large round goggles resting on her head in default art. Yellow mechanic's overalls, tools, goggles, and flight gear support the identity but are not required across skins; use her face and overall character design rather than one accessory.
criteria.Karnok: A rugged male woodsman and monster hunter whose default human form has swept-back black hair, a stern angular face, red eyes, and an enormous dark shaggy fur mantle. He can also appear as his Enraged inner Creature: a dark-furred, snarling beast with large fangs/tusks, luminous teal-green eyes, and vivid pink-magenta energy around the face. Treat the human and beast forms as the same hero; the mantle, colors, and costume are not established as universal across all skins.
criteria.unknown: The character artwork is visible but insufficient, ambiguous, absent, or not one of the eight supported heroes. Do not force a known identity.
criteria.obstructed: The target character artwork is covered by an overlay, webcam or UI enough to prevent identifying the hero. A hidden nameplate alone does not make the hero obstructed.
